title: Planning as Dynamics Relaxation: Hippocampal Recurrent Network Realizes Optimal Goal-Directed Navigation
claim: A single recurrent operator both stores the map and computes the plan by relaxing into a goal-locked field.
layout: 4 panels A–D, left-to-right, maze graph plus plots and heatmaps
description: Four-panel figure with a short title over each panel. Panel A, on the left, shows a grid maze drawn as a node graph. A thick black wall splits it into two rooms. Nodes are colored on a viridis scale, dark purple far from the goal and yellow-green near it. A red-ringed yellow goal node is clamped by a red arrow. A white arrow at the current position y_t points toward the goal. A gold edge marks a synapse written by BTSP. Panel B, at top center, is a log-scale line plot of activity against distance from the goal. Blue curves for increasing times rise toward a dashed black steady-state curve. Panel C, at bottom center, shows a row of field nodes feeding multiplicative readout cells under a Gaussian place kernel, with a bar chart of rates and the formula Δx ∝ Σ∇logψ. Panel D, on the right, has two viridis heatmaps of a two-room maze. The top one is a source query giving the successor field. The bottom one is a clamp query giving the desirability field.
caption: One recurrent operator stores the map and computes the plan. (A) Recurrent place assemblies; a synapse exists only where BTSP wrote an executed transition (gold), so walls write nothing. Recalling a goal clamps one assembly (red); the population relaxes into the goal-locked field $\boldsymbol{\psi}^g$ (node color, log scale), and a readout at the current position $\boldsymbol{y}_t$ points up its log-gradient (white arrow). (B) The activity profile along the route grows out from the clamped goal and converges to the LMDP desirability field (two-room maze, $\alpha=0.985$). (C) Place-tuned readout cells multiply the field by a local place kernel $\mathcal{G}$ centered at $\boldsymbol{y}_t$; their population vector is $\boldsymbol{\Sigma}_G\nabla\log\psi^g$ (Eq. [ref]). (D) Two queries of one operator: a source at the current state yields the successor field (prediction), a clamp at the goal the desirability field (control).
abstract: Neural correlates of the cognitive map are well documented, yet how a neural circuit turns a stored map into an obstacle-avoiding route remains unclear. Here we show that a hippocampal network with appropriate recurrent connections achieves optimal goal-directed navigation through its own relaxation dynamics. The recurrent weights represent the transition probabilities between the locations the neurons encode, walls are reflected by vanishing weights, and behavioral-timescale synaptic plasticity (BTSP) writes this connectivity during goal-free exploration. When a goal is recalled, a top-down current clamps the goal neuron and the population relaxes into a goal-locked activity field. We prove that this field is the desirability field of a linearly-solvable Markov decision process: the relaxed state is the exact optimum of a stated control problem, the KL-regularized objective of Todorov, and the optimal next-step distribution is carried by the branch synaptic currents. The identity extends to directed transitions, and a weak-cost limit returns the Green's function of the recurrent Laplacian. A place-tuned readout converts the field's log-gradient into a direction of travel, and the same synapses answer a predictive query when the source is placed at the current location. Simulations on mazes with complex obstacles show near-shortest routes, an identity that survives a thousand-fold range of recall amplitude, the loss of 80% of place cells, and tens of thousands of states, low-rank updates of every plan after a local change, and a transient that is anytime: the local action is ready long before the field converges. We hope this offers a general circuit principle for planning in abstract cognitive maps beyond spatial navigation.
